t: That wall is straight enough until you stand at the far end.
We are short on pegs again. I counted twice.
The new roof needs another brace before the weather turns.
I saw the lean. We can pull it square tomorrow.
Use the short offcuts for pegs. There is a pile behind the bench.
I would brace both sides. The timber is lighter than usual.
I will reset the corner while you cut the braces.
Measure the doorway before the wall closes around it.
We can settle the rest when the next timber load arrives.
Bring the level tomorrow. I do not trust my eyes tonight.
The stew needs something besides roots, but roots are what we have.
Somebody left the grain sack open again.
I can stretch supper, but I cannot make one fish feed twelve people.
Add more water and cut the roots smaller. Nobody will complain loudly.
I tied that sack myself. Someone opened it after.
Save the fish for the children and fill the rest with grain.
I will check the stores before I promise anything better.
Keep the pot low. Burned stew feeds nobody.
Come back near supper. I will know what we have by then.
We can argue about seasoning after everyone has a bowl.
The eastern trail splits beyond the ridge. Neither branch is marked.
I found running water past the old cairn.
The ground north of here is better than the map suggests.
Take the lower branch. The upper one ends at a steep bank.
Mark the water clearly. A road party will need it.
The map is old. I trust your boots more than the ink.
I will cut a mark where the trail divides.
We should walk it together before sending a loaded party.
Tell me the rest when you have eaten and warmed up.
I will copy your marks before either of us forgets them.
The western row is coming up thin again.
The soil holds water near the fence and nowhere else.
Something has been eating the new shoots overnight.
Replant the gaps and give them more space this time.
Dig a shallow run from the wet corner. It might spread the water.
I saw tracks by the shoots. Small ones, probably birds.
I will cover the weakest row before night.
We should save seed instead of filling every empty patch.
Let us see what survives the week before we change everything.
I will meet you by the field at first light.
The fish moved away from the near bank again.
My net came up with more weed than fish.
The water was cloudy below the crossing this morning.
Try the bend past the reeds. I saw movement there.
Shake the weed out before it dries into the knots.
The rain stirred the bottom. It should clear by tomorrow.
I will mend the wide net if you check the far bend.
We should leave the shallow pools alone for a few days.
Bring your catch to the cook before the afternoon warms it.
I will tell you whether the far bank was worth the walk.
The berry patch beyond the stones is nearly finished.
I found mushrooms under the north trees, but I do not trust all of them.
The baskets are wearing through faster than we can mend them.
Leave the pale mushrooms alone. The darker ones are safe.
There is another berry patch past the creek, smaller but untouched.
Line the weak baskets with cloth until the new ones are ready.
I will mark the safe mushrooms before anyone else finds them.
We should leave enough berries for the bushes to recover.
I will take the creek side tomorrow. You take the stones.
Bring me the torn basket tonight. I can patch it.
I saw wolf tracks near the outer houses.
The south path is too dark after the fires burn low.
Someone should check the gate latch before night.
I will circle the outer houses before supper.
Move one torch closer to the path. That should cover the dark stretch.
The latch held this morning, but I will test it again.
Tell the households to bring children in before dusk.
I would rather check twice than explain one open gate.
I will take the first watch. Wake me if anything changes.
We can compare tracks in daylight. Tonight, keep the spear close.
